disposition_reason: Tables 1-2 print predicted mean Cu, Fe, I, Mn, Mo and Zn in 473 whole pasteurised retail milk samples by production system and month; Hg and Co were below the LOQ in every measurement, while As, Cd, Cr, Ni, Pb, Al and Sn were mostly below the LOQ with no concentrations printed.

study.design: Monthly retail survey, 42 brands of whole pasteurised cow milk over 12 months
study.origin: UK dairy supply (conventional, organic and channel island breed brands)
study.market: retail outlets in South East England
study.method: Lyophilised milk (200 mg) microwave digested (Ultrawave), ICP-MS (Agilent) per NMKL 186; iodine by TMAH dilution ICP-MS
study.lod_text: LOQ per kg milk: Al 174.6, Sn 3.5, As 5.8, Cd 0.6, Cr 5.8, Co 3.5, Hg 3.5, Ni 5.8, Pb 3.5 µg/kg
study.qa: CRMs DORM-5 and skimmed milk powder ERM-BD150 included; technical duplicates; accredited laboratory (Matis)

controls.control: milk production system (organic vs conventional vs channel island breeds)
controls.outcome: Cu 39.0 (CON) vs 37.7 (ORG) vs 46.3 (CHA) µg/kg; Zn 3.59 vs 3.64 vs 4.26 mg/kg; I 326 vs 317 vs 217 µg/kg
I ranged 95 (May) to 451 µg/kg (January); Zn 3.33 (August) to 5.24 mg/kg (February)

unresolved: As, Cd, Cr, Ni, Pb, Al and Sn were mostly below LOQ (As 99.8%, Cd 91.2%, Cr 89.8%, Ni 97.0%, Pb 94.8%, Al 95.4%, Sn 96.0% of measurements) and were not statistically analysed; no concentrations printed in the main text. Values appear only in supplementary Fig. S2, which is not filed next to the PDF.
